t: You're in Leadenhall Market, a covered market on Gracechurch Street, in the middle of the City of London's financial district. It is one of the oldest markets in London, dating from the fourteenth century. The architect here was Sir Horace Jones, who worked for the City of London from 1864 until his death. He was president of the Royal Institute of British Architects from 1882 to 1884 and was knighted in 1886. His most recognised work is Tower Bridge, finished after he died. He is relatively little known, and architects have often marked him down for a perceived lack of artistry.
